liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (3 reviews): Transition slows the groove before building energy, with the crowd reacting intensely; Jerry Garcia sings higher as the crowd becomes increasingly crazy [19][28][30]
- **Althea** (1 review): Listener considers this the best version of the song they have ever heard [20]
- **The Wheel** (1 review): Jam sequence causes intense physical reactions, described as goosebumps and hair loss [25]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Listener calls this version a mind blower and an all-time favorite [30]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-06-18.beyer-m88.morrone.119437.flac2448** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 177 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd83-06-18.aud.gardner.4605.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 171 min; rated 3.93/5 by 14 [4]. Said about its sound: Listener describes the recording quality as crappy in their opinion; Recording quality is not great, but crowd energy is loud and loved [22][28]
- **gd83-06-18.senn421.nawrocki.14411.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 21 songs; 171 min; rated 4.26/5 by 35 [7]. Said about its sound: Vocals are somewhat drowned out by audience noise during the beginning [20]
- **gd1983-06-18.148044.akg.d330bt.senn421.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 168 min; rated 3.67/5 by 3 [9]
- **gd1983-06-18.142271.beyer201.executive-crew.holbrook.flac2448**: audience recording; 20 songs; 158 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [11]
- **gd1983-06-18.154660.S2.Senn441-FRB-PCM-DAT.Silberman-Ammons-Noel.t-flac16**: source not stated; 11 songs; 106 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [15]

## Around the show

- Jerry Garcia displayed significant energy throughout the performance [19]
- Band performed in a somewhat sober state, which the reviewer praises [23]
- Reviewer's first show; energy remains unmatched by later performances despite age [24]
- Crowd arrived from Boston on blotter; Hell's Angels drove bikes near the venue [26]
- Saratoga struggled to handle the influx of people using whippets from gas [27]
- Very unique segue occurs between Morning Dew and Throwing Stones [11]
- A little two-minute jam occurs between Fire on the Mountain and Playin' [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-06-18.beyer-m88.morrone.119437.flac2448**: taped by Joe Morrone; transferred by Andrew F.; source: AUD: 2x Beyer M-88's > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX-90s, recorded from inside the pavilion, directly behind the soundboard area, taped by Joe Morrone. [1]. Also: P.A. mix improves after the first two songs; patches from other sources [1]
- **gd83-06-18.aud.gardner.4605.sbeok.shnf**: source: Sennheiser 421's> Sony D-5 taped by Jim Wise [4]
- **gd83-06-18.senn421.nawrocki.14411.sbeok.shnf**: source: Sennheiser 421's> Sony D-5 taped by Jim Wise [7]
- **gd1983-06-18.148044.akg.d330bt.senn421.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Chris Hecht; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Chris Hecht's Master Audience Cassettes; (2) AKG D330BT mics + (1) Sennheiser 421 > Fostex Mixer > Sony D5M [9]. Also: Sennheiser 421 source supplies crowd, Bertha start, Deal end, and patches [9]
- **gd1983-06-18.142271.beyer201.executive-crew.holbrook.flac2448**: taped by Executive Crew Fran Walsh Kyle Holbrook Mike Yacavone Olvy Johnson Rick Cantor; transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: flac24/48 Master: AUD MC Beyer M201's X-Y 8'up > Sony TCD5M no dolby Maxell MX90 x 2.First Gen patch: [Same mics]Sony TCD5M no dolby Maxell UDXLII 90Cassette… [11]. Also: Master tape overtaped from Big River through Althea due to side swap error [11]
- **gd1983-06-18.154660.S2.Senn441-FRB-PCM-DAT.Silberman-Ammons-Noel.t-flac16**: taped by Recorded by Jeff Silberman PCM to DAT Transfer by Jeff Silberman; transferred by DAT Transfer by John Ammons Edited & Mastered (Adobe Audition) by Joe Noel November 05, 2021; source: Source: Sennheiser 441 > Technics 14 bit PCM > DAT Location: Front Row Balcony [15]. Also: Jeff did not record the first set to protect new digital gear from rain [15]

claims.text: Transition slows the groove before building energy, with the crowd reacting intensely
Jerry Garcia displayed significant energy throughout the performance
Listener considers this the best version of the song they have ever heard
Vocals are somewhat drowned out by audience noise during the beginning
Listener describes the recording quality as crappy in their opinion
Band performed in a somewhat sober state, which the reviewer praises
Reviewer's first show; energy remains unmatched by later performances despite age
Jam sequence causes intense physical reactions, described as goosebumps and hair loss
Crowd arrived from Boston on blotter; Hell's Angels drove bikes near the venue
Saratoga struggled to handle the influx of people using whippets from gas
Jerry Garcia sings higher as the crowd becomes increasingly crazy
Recording quality is not great, but crowd energy is loud and loved
Most rowdy and powerful version; band nearly stops before timing tweaks
Listener calls this version a mind blower and an all-time favorite
P.A. mix improves after the first two songs; patches from other sources
Thanks Chris Hecht for master; Charlie Miller for transfer and coordination
Sennheiser 421 source supplies crowd, Bertha start, Deal end, and patches
Master tape overtaped from Big River through Althea due to side swap error
Very unique segue occurs between Morning Dew and Throwing Stones
Jeff did not record the first set to protect new digital gear from rain
A little two-minute jam occurs between Fire on the Mountain and Playin'
